question: May I store customer contracts in a public AI service?
answer:
Based on the provided source passages, the answer is:

No, you may not store customer contracts in a public AI service. According to [NL-14:S1], customer contracts are classified as confidential data. According to [NL-14:S2], confidential data may only be stored in approved company systems, and publicly accessible AI services are not an approved storage location for confidential data.

Additionally, [NL-03:S1] states that personal devices must not access internal customer data, which suggests that storing customer contracts in a public AI service would be a violation of this rule.

sources.title: Data Classification
sources.heading: Handling
sources.text: Confidential data may be stored only in approved company systems. Sharing it with external recipients requires data owner approval. Publicly accessible AI services are not an approved storage location for confidential data.

sources.title: Data Classification
sources.heading: Classes
sources.text: The classification levels are public, internal and confidential. Customer contracts, credentials and personal customer data are confidential. Published product brochures are public. Internal process descriptions are internal.

sources.title: Company Handbook
sources.heading: Contacts
sources.text: People Operations handles working arrangements and onboarding. IT Operations handles devices and access. Finance processes expense claims. Requests are submitted through the internal service portal. Never include passwords in a ticket.

sources.title: Knowledge Platform Backup Plan
sources.heading: Retention
sources.text: Backups of the internal knowledge platform are retained for 60 calendar days. Security reviews the plan annually. This retention statement does not concern Atlas customer data.

sources.title: Standard IT Equipment
sources.heading: Devices
sources.text: Standard equipment includes a managed laptop, a headset and one external monitor. Personal devices must not access internal customer data. The laptop remains company property.
